Why did Meta do this?
Meta made some strange and unexpected changes to video custom audiences. Let’s take a closer look…
The Change
When you create a video custom audience, you now have three options…
- All Video Viewers: People who watched at least 3 seconds of your video.
- Engaged Video Viewers: People who watched a meaningful portion of your video.
- Highly Engaged Video Viewers: People who watched most or all of your video.
Previously, there were seven options:
- 3 seconds
- 10 seconds
- 15 seconds
- 25% of the video
- 50% of the video
- 75% of the video
- 95% of the video
There isn’t any new functionality with this change. If anything, it’s far less clear what each selection means. What is a “meaningful portion”? And how is that different from “most” of your video? I assume this will be clarified eventually in Meta’s documentation, but for now it’s a mystery.
Unfortunately, this update doesn’t even add something that’s been needed for years. You still have to select individual videos that the custom audience applies to. There isn’t an option to create an audience of all video views.
Why Now?
So, why is Meta doing this now? Is anyone using video custom audiences these days?
These are some of the lowest-quality custom audiences you can create. It’s far too easy to get a long view of a video by accident with auto-play on. And there are ad placements (Audience Network Rewarded Video) that force or incentivize longer views.
In other words, a view of your video does not necessarily suggest intent. I would not advise separate remarketing of these audiences, and Meta will remarket to these people automatically if they’re a strong prospect anyway.
Simplifying is a good thing, but I’m not sure why this was a priority. It seems like there are far more important things Meta should be worrying about right now.
